summary: Enumerated all ES solutions for primes p<=3000 (divisor method, validated against the f4 U-data for n<3000) and recorded the Legendre pattern of (x,y,z) mod l, l=3,5,7, for denominators prime to l. Every locally allowed unordered pattern (from 4uvw = p(uv+vw+wu) mod l) occurs globally (l=3: 2/2 patterns, l=5: 4/4, l=7: 4/4), so no hidden sign constraint shows up at these moduli. Caveat: patterns are sorted, so ordering information is discarded.

Closure check: the N-span of 1, i, j, k is not multiplicatively closed since i*i = -1 has a negative coefficient (PROVED). So the cone has to be designed differently; no ES test was needed to reach this.

Cone not fixed by the item (maximal real subfield Q(sqrt2) inside Z[zeta8]). Spec: fix the cone as totally positive in Q(sqrt2) (elements of Z[zeta8] whose two real embeddings of the Q(sqrt2)-part are positive, plus a height filter), then search 4/n = sum of 3 cone unit fractions for n <= 200 with element height <= 30 (about 10^5 candidates; cheap in exact arithmetic).
next: Re-run with a fixed cone; first check whether the unit eps = 1+sqrt2 (norm -1) is needed at all.

summary: H00's exhaustive Gaussian-cone search (outcome_H00 Z0067; closed-Q1 cone, N(n)<=4000) already answers the square question: its 12 exceptions include the Gaussian square 3+4i = (2+i)^2, and the others are non-squares of norm <= 293. Nothing new beyond that record.

Closure check by hand: (eps+i)^2 = eps^2-1+2 eps i has Re<0 for 0<eps<1, so the closed first quadrant {Re>0, Im>=0} is not multiplicatively closed (PROVED). The cone question was settled by H00's Z0067 search for the closed-Q1 cone, which contains ES exactly as its real slice.
Closed: Q_p has no order compatible with its field structure, so 'positivity via an embedding into R' is not defined on Z_p. Category error; no step to run.
First step is reading Boyd's p-adic harmonic-sum paper (not in repo, not verified here); no ES-specific question is stated, and the item itself marks it low priority.
r_T(n) = #{(a,b,c) >= 0 : T_a + T_b + T_c = n} (Gauss three triangular numbers) vs residual log U on n in [100, 3000] with U>0 (2901 values): correlation -0.07, log version -0.06. Negligible.
The first step needs a map from a totally positive cyclotomic unit eta (eta = -1 mod an inert prime) to an ES solution, and the item gives no such map. Not executable as stated.

Repo already has the numerics (data/z52b/analogues_constraints4_fails_8000.json, 499 primes = 1 mod 4 below 8000). I re-ran the check to p<3000 (211 primes, 0 repeated-denominator solutions) and wrote an elementary PROVED lemma: x=y forces (4x-2p)(4z-p) = 2p^2; B = 4z-p is odd and = 3 (mod 4) for p = 1 (mod 4); the only admissible negative B > -p is B=-1, which gives x<0; positive odd divisors of 2p^2 are = 1 (mod 4). The case y=z is symmetric.

For u = -omega^2 one has u^2 = u - 1, so the semiring N[1,u] is not multiplicatively closed (PROVED). The first step (test closure of candidate cones) rules this cone out; other small unit cones were not enumerated.

Closed first-quadrant cone (Re>0, Im>=0, as in H00 Z0067), Gaussian denominators of norm <= 100, three-term sums for p = 41 and p = 137: no solution found. Height-limited negative; not evidence against existence at larger height.
next: Repeat at norm bound 300 (the search is O(#elements^2)).

summary: Gaussian primes pi of norm <= 300 (59) with 4/pi = 1/x + 1/y + 1/alpha, x,y <= 200 rational integers, alpha in Z[i]: 2 of 59 have a solution, e.g. 4/(4+i) = 1/2 + 1/2 + 1/(-1+4i) (checked exactly). Sparse; no structure beyond this.
Record-only item: the first step is deferred by the item itself to batch B ('quadratic orbit ES'). Nothing to test here.

Exact search for 4/n = sum of three terms 1/(c s_i^2), c in {1,2,3,5,6}, n <= 1500 (bounds: c s1^2 <= 3n/4 and s2^2 <= 2/(c*rem)). Hits: c=1: 50 (3.3%), c=2: 30 (2.0%), c=3: 55 (3.7%), c=5: 19 (1.3%), c=6: 35 (2.3%). Every hit has 4 | n, consistent with H00's Z0142 (4/n = sum 1/a_i^2 forces 4|n). No coset-level obstruction beyond the 4-adic one showed up.
Closed: Z[i]^x is finite (order 4), so there are no infinite-order units and no norm-one torus of the stated kind. The premise fails.

Z[i] solutions of 4/p with all denominators of norm <= 50, p < 50 (13 primes): 522 denominators; octant histogram concentrated near the positive real axis (181 in [0,45) deg, 97 in [315,360)). A height effect, not equidistribution; angles of unbounded solutions are not defined by this search.

Finite-height existence only: Z[i] solutions of 4/p with all norms <= 25 exist for 10 of 22 primes p<90 (fail at 29,31,37,...). The sector-fraction part of the item was NOT run; the result is H-dependent and only indicative.
next: Run the sector fraction for H = 25, 50, 100 to check stability.

summary: (1+i)^k/pi for k=1,2,3 and all Gaussian primes pi with norm <= 61 (34 primes) are each a sum of three Z[i] unit fractions with norms <= 25 (34/34 for every k). Not discriminating at this height.

Finite-height search (norm <= 25) for 4/p as a sum of three unit fractions, p<90 (22 primes): solvable counts Z[i] 10, Z[omega] 10, Z[sqrt2] 15, Z[(1+sqrt-7)/2] 9. These are height-limited counts, not cone-closed failure statistics; the comparison is indicative only.
next: Repeat with norm bounds 50 and 100 to see whether the ranking is stable.

summary: Z[sqrt2] with four cones (rational, N[sqrt2], height-positive, totally positive), norms <= 25, p<90 (22 primes): solvable for 2, 5, 5, 2 primes respectively. Height-limited; no separation between cones at this bound.
NOT RUN in fix pass: Hurwitz-quaternion search not implemented (the fix rule requires a concrete run; this item remains open).
Category error: there is no ordering of Q_p compatible with multiplication, so 'absolute value positivity' does not give a cone. Closed.
Denominators a*2^k (a<=15, k<=12) alone solve 4/p for only 4 of 166 primes p<1000; adding p times them solves 126 of 166. The p-multiples are forced, since p | xyz for every solution.

Lucas-divisibility test: 4Cp+1 divides some U_k(P,Q) with |P|,|Q| <= 3, k <= 60 for 404 of 1450 (C,p) pairs (28%). The random control (N = 1 mod 4 in [1e4, 6e5]) gives 100%, which contradicts the ES rate, so the test as set up is not informative. Needs a corrected control and a rank-of-apparition argument.
next: Use rank-of-apparition to decide divisibility exactly instead of sampling k <= 60.

Lift test: 4/n = 2Re(xi)/N(xi) + 1/z with n = N(pi) prime = 1 mod 4 (n <= 200, 21 primes), |a|<=40, b<=40: 19 of 21 have a lift, but z is often 1 (e.g. 4/5 = -1/5 + 1), so the lifts are trivial at this height. Nothing usable.

Computed, for C<=12 and all primes p=1 mod 4 up to 2e4, the subgroup H_C generated by the prime factors of 4Cp+1 mod 4C. -1 is outside H_C for 28% (C=1), 56% (C=2), 71% (C=3), 86% (C=6) of primes. This is only a sufficient condition for the C-slice to fail (no divisor can be -1 mod 4C); it gives no lever on ES, since the slices fail often and ES still holds through other C.

The statement as written is false: for every prime p=3 mod 4 the curve y^2=x^3-x has a_p=0 (checked to 1200), so a_p mod 8 cannot equal (2/p) = +-1. The correct form holds in range: for p=1 mod 4 (95 primes below 1200), a_p/2 mod 4 equals (2/p) mapped to 1 or 3 in all 95 cases. Sanity check only.

Regression of residual log U on log|L(1,chi_D)| for D in {p,-4p,-8p,-3p,5p,-7p}, p=1 mod 4 below 1000 (n=69): R^2 = 0.59. Legendre symbols (2/p),(-3/p),(5/p),(-7/p) alone give R^2 = 0.60, and together with the L-values 0.64. The L-values add nothing beyond the quadratic characters; d=-3 has the largest drop only because (-3/p) is included.

Repeated the check for primes q<=50 with cubic (order 3) and quartic (order 4) residue classes after removing the quadratic-character stratum of q: within-stratum F<=3.49 for all 30 tests (df 2,1597), about chance for 30 tests. The unstratified F (e.g. 2 quartic: 365) is the (2/p) effect.

2-adic solution density rho_k(p) = #{(x,y,z) mod 2^k : 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) mod 2^k}/2^{2k}: rho(17) = rho(9) exactly for k = 3, 4, 5 (1.25, 1.375, 1.375), ratio 1.0. The naive local density of this equation does not depend on p mod 16, so the 9% gap is not a local density effect of this equation.

higher_residue.json already has the test: quartic residuosity of 2 (stratified mean diff 0.0079, Mann-Whitney p=0.088). I reproduced it within the quadratic strata (F=0.17, df 2,1597) for q=2, order 4.
classical_corr.txt already reports the Spearman correlation of U(p) with h(p) (about -0.04 in the item). No new computation was made for this item.
Verified r3(p) = 12 h(-4p) exactly for p=1 mod 4 up to 2000 (60 primes sampled, max error 1e-13; class numbers via the L(1,chi_D) formula). The correlation step is in Z0798.

Regression of residual log U on log H(4p)/sqrt p, log H(8p)/sqrt p, log H(3p)/sqrt p for p=1 mod 4 below 2000: R^2 = 0.53 (coeffs 0.36, 0.07, 0.42). Caveat: this is largely the quadratic-character effect of Z0701 (the h(-3p) term tracks (-3/p)); not controlled here.
next: Control for Legendre symbols (2/p),(-3/p) before reading any class-number signal.

summary: Partial Spearman of residual log U with ord_p(b)/(p-1), controlling (2/p) and tau(p-1), p=1 mod 4 in (100,30000] (n=1600): base 2: 0.19 (raw 0.46); base 3: 0.39; base 5: 0.27. Base 2 is not special.
Fermat quotient q_p(2) normalised to [0,1): Spearman with residual log U -0.05 (partial given log p -0.05), p=1 mod 4 below 3e4. Negligible.

Proth primes k*2^n+1 up to 1e8: U(p) by the divisor method costs O(p) per x (about 3e7 x-values at 1e8), infeasible within 30 min. Needs an O(sqrt p)-per-x method or a lattice method, i.e. more than 1 h coding.

PROVED.

U(409) = 15 and U(577) = 18, so neither is a zero of the ES count; the repo's R-zero notion is not reproduced by U. Primes near the Pell-related numbers (2377, 2381, 13873, 19597, 19609) checked for membership; no R-zero pattern tested beyond that.

summary: Tunnell counts A(p)=r_{1,2,8}(p), B(p)=r_{1,2,32}(p) for p<=3e4: corr(resU, A-2B) = +0.02 (matches the item's null); corr(resU, A) = -0.52 (log count). A(p)=0 for all p=5 mod 8 and never for p=1 mod 8, so the raw correlation is a mod-8 split (see Z0968). The item's rank of y^2=x^3-p^2x is 0 identically (squares are not congruent), so the curve was taken as the Tunnell n=p form.

Composite n <= 30000 (26721 with U>0). Partial correlation (after regressing residual log U on log n, log log n) with r_{x^2+y^2}(n): -0.11 (raw count), -0.17 (log count); r_{x^2+2y^2}: -0.05 / -0.14; r_{x^2+3y^2}: +0.02 / -0.06. These modest negative correlations may just reflect the divisor structure of n (not controlled here); no clean signal.

Within p=1 mod 8 and after controlling (2/p), h(-8p), h(-4p), the Tunnell count A(p) keeps a positive partial correlation with residual log U: +0.30 (A) and +0.30 (B) for p<2000 (n~300). Raw correlations are -0.31 (A) and -0.30 (B), a sign reversal driven by the mod-8 split. The item's rho=+0.18 was NOT reproduced (its definitions differ). A-2B is null (-0.08).
next: Check the item's definitions of A and B against final_checks.json; if the +0.30 survives in the item's own data, test whether it is a class-number-free 2-adic effect by splitting p mod 16.

Jacobi reciprocity gives prod over q|N of (-p/q) (with multiplicity) = (-p/N) for N = 4Cp+1, which is determined by N mod 4p and reciprocity (PROVED, classical). The identity is standard and I did not re-read the T1 template to check it is already used there.

The subgroup test says 'contains -1' but no divisor realises it in 521 cases (13.0%), so containment is necessary, not sufficient, for a divisor. The 'no -1 in subgroup' direction is exact.

Type I hits (divisor f | p^2+4c^2 d with f = -p mod 4cd) over c <= 60 for 10 primes near 1e4: d=1: 0 hits, d=2: 72, d=3: 24, d=5: 20, d=7: 19. The class-number main term h(-4d) log X would predict d=1 is nonzero (h(-4) = 1 is smallest), yet the count is exactly zero. Consistent with Z3030 (0 of 1600 pairs at d=1). A genuine surprise relative to the class-number heuristic.

Abstract read (arXiv 2404.08380): GRH-conditional Fourier optimisation for least quadratic non-residue and least prime in AP. The repo's classical_corr.txt already reports U(p) ~ least QNR (-0.66), so the signal is covered; no new bound was derived.

Classical fact: Q(i)/Q is cyclic, so the Hasse norm theorem holds, and solvability of N(alpha)=m over Q(i) is decided by local conditions. Hence the norm-form side has no global obstruction beyond local ones (PROVED, standard).
Source is an unverified search URL; no Pell parameterisation is given.
Source is an unverified search URL; the 'complementary failure sets' test needs the family list first.
Source is an unverified search URL; the list of ES quadratic forms is not given.
Abstract read (arXiv 1604.06723, Sun): refinements of Lagrange's four-square theorem with a square or cube condition on linear combinations. No link to the ES equation identified.

Regressed residual log U (p=1 mod 4, p<=1500) on class numbers h(-Dp), D in {3,4,7,8}: R^2 = 0.027 for the sum over sqrt(p), 0.01-0.06 for single D except D=3 (0.34). h(-3p) carries the (-3/p) Legendre effect; Legendre symbols (2/p),(-3/p),(5/p),(-7/p) alone give R^2 = 0.63. No exact class-number relation found.

Web search confirmed Heath-Brown, Primes represented by x^3+2y^3, Acta Math. 186 (2001). Its method is cubic-residue parity for a cubic form; the Type I norm N(p+2c sqrt(-d)) = p^2+4c^2 d is quadratic in p with discriminant -16c^2 d, so no cubic-parity transfer is available. Ray-class translation not computed.

Maynard arXiv:1507.05080 (read abstract): incomplete norm-form prime values need n >= 4k with k >= 1 incomplete coefficients. For Q(sqrt(-d)), n=2 < 4, so the theorem does not apply to the ES norm forms (PROVED by the stated hypothesis).

Browning–Matthiesen arXiv:1307.7641 (read abstract): N_K(k) = P(t) with P split into linear factors over Q. For p^2+4c^2 d as a polynomial in p the discriminant -16c^2 d is not a square, so P does not split over Q and the BM setting does not apply.

Abstract read (arXiv 1807.02721): an alternative proof of Faltings via p-adic period maps. For the ES surface, the slice with z fixed is {4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx)} in (x,y), a (1,1)-curve, which has genus 0. A higher-genus curve needs two simultaneous conditions; not constructed.

Bounded check: all 426 S-smooth n <= 20000 have at least one solution with all three denominators S-smooth (S={2,3,5,7}), so the search is saturated at this height and says nothing about finiteness. Baker/Chabauty not attempted.

Bounded brute force (the step as stated): all S-smooth n <= 20000 with S={2,3,5,7} have an all-S-smooth solution (426/426), so the search is saturated and gives no finiteness information. Chabauty/Baker not attempted (see Z2615).

Spec: for hard p and d, c small, compute the class of each prime divisor of p^2+4c^2 d in the form class group of disc -16c^2 d (form-enumeration as in Z2491), and test whether the Type-I failure set correlates with class parity. The Type-I failure definition must first be fixed (see Z1438). Coding about 1 h; exceeds the 30-min rule.
next: Fix the Type-I definition, then implement the class-of-divisor map.

summary: Read EVW arXiv:1212.0923 (Cohen–Lenstra over function fields via homological stability): it gives the distribution of class groups of function fields in Hurwitz families. Identifying which function-field class groups enter the Type I count was not done, so no 2-part is computed.
Abstract read (arXiv 2207.05674, Smith): distribution of l-infinity Selmer groups in degree-l twist families. The Rédei-matrix sterility model for ES was NOT computed.
Abstract read (arXiv 2201.13424, Koymans–Pagano): Rédei-type reciprocity for multiquadratic class groups and reflection principles. The e-slice as a class of -1 was not computed.

Abstract read (arXiv 1908.01752, CKMP): negative Pell solubility via Smith's 2-Selmer/class-group distributions (improving Fouvry-Kluners). The step converting rank distributions into a proportion lower bound was not checked in the body of the paper.

For D=-16d, d<=100: reduced forms enumerated; primes q<=100 split in D are assigned to classes via small representations. Mean fraction of classes hit = 0.61; full coverage for only 11 of 100 values of d. Small split primes do not reach all classes of disc -16d at this height.

Read Cluckers–Loeser arXiv math/0410203 (abstract). Computing sigma_l(n) symbolically for the Cayley-cubic model needs a motivic-integration implementation (or a manual cell decomposition); estimated > 1 h coding, beyond the 30-min rule.
next: Fix the Cayley-cubic local model and count points mod l^k by brute force first; the symbolic step is the expensive part.

summary: Duke 1988 (Invent. Math. 92) is not on arXiv; the OAI-015 claim could not be verified from an accessible source.

The identity sum_chi conj(chi)(-1) sum_{d|N} chi(d) = phi(m) #{d|N : d = -1 mod m} is character orthogonality (checked by hand); the principal-character term is tau(N)/phi(4C). Its consequence, that divisor pairs d <-> N/d force evenness of the count (Z3130), was checked on 1764 pairs with zero violations. Nothing beyond the standard identity.
Abstract read (arXiv 2109.15230, Nelson): t-aspect subconvexity for standard L-functions. Positivity of class-group L(1) sums needs a bound at the edge, which this does not give.

Abstract read (arXiv 1904.00290, LMMS): effective avoidance for unipotent orbits. The ES equation 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) is not a fixed homogeneous form equal to a constant, so the counting theorem does not apply directly.

A twisted Dedekind sum with character mod 4C whose reciprocity is chi-sensitive must first be defined (Rademacher–Grosswald §3 twisted sums); designing and testing it on ES certificates is more than 30 min of coding.
next: Write the twisted Dedekind-sum definition from Rademacher–Grosswald and test reciprocity on small moduli.

summary: P(-1 is a divisor residue | some prime factor of N has maximal order mod 4C) = 0.163 vs 0.036 without (C<=20, p<1500). The enrichment is a divisor-count confound: stratified by tau(N), the two probabilities coincide (e.g. tau=4: 0.079 vs 0.079; tau=12: 0.305 vs 0.286). OAI-029 claim not verified (not an accessible source).
Only the bounded search of Z2478 was run (n<=20000); the Baker/LLL full solution was NOT attempted (needs a Matveev-bound implementation; beyond 30 min).

I3 is defined in the repo's I3 notes (EXSET_I3.md, I3_DEEP_ASTRA); identifying its binary-form family and discriminant needs that definition extracted and checked. Reading and checking is more than 30 min; not done.
next: Extract I3(t,n) from I3_DEEP_ASTRA §8 and test which binary form of disc t^2 n^2 + ... it represents.

summary: Enumerating reduced ternary forms of det p in each genus with Eisenstein reduction, for p<2000, and checking chain bases requires ternary reduction and genus enumeration (> 1 h coding); the Brandt–Intrau tables are not available in the repo.
next: Implement ternary reduction and genus splitting for p < 300 first.

summary: Testing representability of binary forms of disc up to X by ternary forms of det p in the non-square genus needs the same genus machinery as Z2666 (> 1 h).
next: Depends on Z2666.

summary: Expressing the CM-order collision count as Hecke correspondence intersections (Gross–Keating) needs Hecke correspondence code on Gross–Keating's setting (> 1 h coding).
next: Implement the quaternion Hecke correspondence for small p.

summary: The fixed ternary form and sign condition must first be extracted from QUATERNION_ES (Lambda_{d,m}); then DSP effectivity needs a representation count check (> 30 min including the reformulation).
next: Extract the form from QUATERNION_ES and count representations of p-tied numbers.

summary: Regressed residual log U on log h(-Dp), D in {3,4,7,8}, p<1500: R^2 = 0.49 with coefficients (0.38, 0.07, -0.02, -0.24). h(-3p) dominates through the (-3/p) Legendre effect; once (2/p),(-3/p),(5/p),(-7/p) are included the class numbers add nothing (Z2365). No positive combination with an exact class-number identity found.

M_t^lev(n) and sums of Hurwitz numbers H(4tn - s^2) over s and t need Hurwitz numbers at non-fundamental discriminants (orders, weights), which the L(1,chi_D) route does not give directly; implementing this is > 30 min.
next: Implement H(D) via reduced forms of all orders and compare for n < 1000 first.

summary: Calibrating box size against narrow class numbers in Z[2 sqrt f] needs narrow class group computation and GRH-Bach bounds (> 1 h coding).
The certificate region for CM points of disc -4p has to be defined (LATTICE_MEETING.md) and its hyperbolic area computed; more than 30 min.

Class number of Q(sqrt(-p)) (disc -4p) mod 8 vs residual log U (p<1500, n~100): residual means +0.16 (h = 2 mod 8), -0.24 (4), +0.26 (6), -0.26 (0). These track the (2/p) split (h = 2 mod 4 iff p = 5 mod 8). No genus-character signal beyond (2/p). Rédei-matrix 4-rank not computed separately.
Gross lattice (trace-zero part) of Lambda_{d,m} for (d,m) <= 20 and its genus need quaternion-order arithmetic (> 1 h coding).

Over p=1 mod 4 below 3000 (211 primes), the 211 x 20 F2-matrix of slice-success bits (C=1..20) has rank 20: no F2-linear relation among slice successes (codimension 0). Failure space is full in this range.
Borwein–Choi (Exp. Math. 9 (2000)): at most 19 integers are not of the form xy+yz+zx with x,y,z >= 1 (web-search abstract). The class-group translation to I3 was not done.
Testing whether I3 failures force small class-group exponent needs the I3 exceptional list (in the repo's I3 notes) and class groups of orders of disc -D(n); > 30 min.
next: Extract the I3 exception list and compute class group exponents of disc -D(n) for small n.

summary: Norm of (1-zeta^A)/(1-zeta) to Q(sqrt p) sign-sensitivity needs cyclotomic-unit norm computations for many p; the item gives no target identity. Estimated > 1 h to design and test.
next: Fix the target identity, then compute norms for p < 200.

summary: Checking Type I existence against N(j(tau_1) - j(tau_2)) requires singular-moduli values for the orders of Lambda_{d,m}; > 1 h without a CM library.
Not run: 2-adic measure of words with pentagon entries divisible by 4 needs the BM_CORRECTED_COUNT word model; not implemented in this pass.
Not run: needs the Hilbert 1909 universal-form map translated to ES triples; this is a restatement-level step with no executable definition in the item.
Abstract read (arXiv 1512.01565, BDG): main conjecture in Vinogradov's MVT via decoupling. No congruencing analogue for the (u,B) count was built.
The lattice reformulations to test are not enumerated in the repo's list; genus class numbers need Sage/Magma; > 1 h.

Partial correlations of residual log U with class numbers: h(-4p) alone R^2 = 0.011; h(-3p) alone 0.34 (Legendre confound); L(1,chi_p) corr -0.74 with residual (p<=1000). With Legendre symbols the class numbers add nothing. Correlations use the residual U, since f_I is not defined in the item.

F_p(C,a) = 1[a mod 4C is a divisor class of 4Cp+1] over unit classes a mod 4C (C<=12, p=1 mod 4 < 2000): F(a)F(b) = F(ab) holds for 79.7% of triples. F is not character-like; no profinite multiplicativity.

Indicator matrix over 147 primes (p=1 mod 4 < 2000) with columns (C,a), C<=12: rank 81 of 126 columns, so 45 rational linear relations hold on the sample. Relations not identified (an involution d -> N/d pairs classes a and a^{-1} in counts); no test on new primes yet.
next: Identify the 45 relations and test them on primes not in the sample.

summary: Log-mass fraction of 4Cp+1 carried by prime factors q not = +-1 mod 4C: mean 0.63 (C<=12, p<2000). No separation test against slice success done.

Explained variance of residual log U (p=1 mod 4, 100<p<=3e4) by residue-class indicators mod q, cumulative over q: out-of-sample R^2 rises 0.09 (q=3), 0.57 (q=8), 0.63 (q=16-23), 0.73 (q=24). The conductor-24 step is the quadratic character (6/p) = (2/p)(3/p), the interaction term missing from an additive Legendre model: on the mod-8 + mod-3 base it adds +0.06 out of sample (0.421 -> 0.478), with corr(residual, (6/p)) = -0.26. This term is absent from the repo (grep for (6/p), (2/p)(3/p): no hits).
next: Test whether the (2/p)(3/p) interaction survives with all Legendre symbols and class numbers included, on primes up to 1e5 (pr_1e5 data), before reading it as a real term.

summary: Expressing the SL2-form certificate condition as a class-function count in SL2(Z/q) and expanding by Frobenius' formula needs character tables of SL2(Z/q) and a precise certificate-to-matrix encoding (the item does not give one). Designing and verifying this is more than 1 h of coding, beyond the 30-min rule.
next: Define the SL2 encoding of a certificate, then compute the character table of SL2(Z/q) for q <= 50 and the Frobenius expansion.

summary: Abstract read (arXiv 2003.02592, Machiavelo–Tsopanidis): quaternion arithmetic in Lipschitz integers for Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture. The constrained-quaternion-norm version for ES was not attempted.
Divisors f of p^2+4c^2 with f = -p mod 4c: zero of 1600 pairs (p=1 mod 4 < 1000, c<=20). This is the T1 exclusion at a square-type norm (FRONTIER §1 T1), reproduced numerically.

Mordell triples xy+yz+zx = p (positive): p does not divide xyz for any positive solution (if p | x then xy+yz+zx > p), so the map 4xyz/p = n never yields an integer n. The transform gives no ES solution. PROVED.
Norms of singular-moduli differences or Weber values for small p need CM j-invariants (pari or Sage); not available in this environment; > 30 min.
Class numbers of Eichler orders of level 4C in the Hurwitz algebra need Sage/Magma; > 1 h without them.

At N = 4C m^2 + 1 for odd m (C<=25, 975 pairs) no proper divisor is -1 mod 4C: failure rate 1.0 (versus 0.90 for N = 4Cp+1). This is the odd-square exclusion (T1; FRONTIER §1, M_BM(m^2) = 0). The local-condition explanation at 2 and at primes dividing C was not separately tested.
Fitting sub-route failure sets to reciprocity conditions needs the repo's census data and sub-route definitions (> 1 h).
Searching kappa(p) invariants over p <= 1e8 for ES-guarantee correlations needs a fast U(p) at 1e8 (see Z0814): > 1 h.
Representations of Mordell-hard primes by principal-genus forms of disc dividing -4*840 need the certificate list (u,B,C) and genus character code (> 1 h).

Parity of the divisor count M(N,C) = #{d|N : d = -1 mod 4C}: d -> N/d maps the class -1 to itself (since N = 1 mod 4C), so M is even unless N is a square. Verified on 1764 (C,p) pairs, 0 violations. This is the trivial involution, not an Eisenstein congruence beyond mod 2.
X(p) and M_gen are defined in the repo's notes (not in this batch); bounding |X(p)| by character sums needs those definitions; > 30 min.
Testing representability of sporadic exceptions by all reduced positive ternary forms of disc <= 500 needs ternary form enumeration and reduction (> 1 h coding).

Distribution of least certificate C_min (divisor version) mod 8 and mod 3 over 609 primes below 1e4: dominated by C_min=1 (439 primes, residue 1 mod 8). No Fourier-type structure beyond that; Tao's Collatz analogue (arXiv:1909.03562, abstract read) uses entropy, not applicable directly.

Located Katz, Gauss Sums, Kloosterman Sums and Monodromy Groups (princeton PDF). The Type II exponential sum is a Salié sum with closed form (BRAINSTORM/y3_salie_angle.md, verified on 300 certificates), so its monodromy is not needed. FUNCTIONFIELD_ES §4 contains no Salié sum.

Sawin–Shusterman arXiv:1808.04001 (read abstract): improved function-field Burgess bound; level of distribution close to 1 for Möbius over F_q[T] on special subspaces. The item's map to ES Type I (P-tied polynomials in progressions with modulus degree > deg/2) was not established.

Same paper (1808.04001): Möbius over F_q[T] is mimicked by Dirichlet characters on special subspaces. Whether the FF ES counting function at fixed P has a Möbius/Liouville twist is not checked; parity-barrier relation not established.
Abstract read (arXiv 1111.2574): exceptional set for the two-term equation a/n = 1/x + 1/y. ES is three-term; the extension of the method was not attempted.
Abstract read (arXiv math/9904181, Croot): every rational r is a sum of unit fractions with denominators in (N, e^r N). Gives no three-term window for ES.
Nearest other 3-term sum to 4/p, with x,y,z<=120 (about 3e5 sums): distances ~1e-5 to 2e-3 for p<120, mean 9e-5, i.e. about the mean spacing. No accumulation signal.

Hooley Delta on N=4Cp+1 (C in 1,6,...,46; 60 primes each) has mean 1.48, versus 2.33 for random N in [1e5,1e6]. The control is not matched (random N are not 1 mod 4 and not from the family), so the gap is not interpreted.

For n=pq with p,q=1 mod 4 below 100 (55 pairs): every solution of 4/(pq) has some denominator divisible by p, which is forced because p | xyz for every ES solution (4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx)). The 'prescribed distribution' is therefore automatic; nothing beyond this lemma.
Beatty denominators floor(k*theta), theta in {sqrt2, golden, e/2}, with three-term sums, p<1000 (166 primes): solvable for 35, 34, 34 primes respectively. No sign of a special set.
Elsholtz–Tao arXiv:1107.1010 (read abstract): sum_{p<=N} f(p) of order N log^2 N. Here mean U(p)/log^2 p = 0.97 (median 0.97, sd 0.30) over p=1 mod 4, p<=3e4, matching the box-volume heuristic.
Meta: the item says 'Low priority; note' and proposes no test; no ES-specific step is defined, so there is nothing to execute (rule 3: meta/organisational item).

Histogram of x/p over all ES solutions for p=1 mod 4 below 1500 (3498 solutions): 84% of mass lies in [0.25,0.30), decaying above. This is the expected concentration just above p/4 and carries no hidden angular law.
U(n) = 1 occurs only at n=2 among n <= 3000 (U minimum), so there is no sporadic set of composites to factor; class numbers for n <= 3000 with U <= 2 were not tabulated. Nothing found.

classical_corr.txt already has U(p) ~ L(1,chi_p) (-0.69 Spearman). Re-run: residual log U vs log L(1,chi_p) (p<=1000): coefficient -0.45, corr -0.74 (n=69), largely the Legendre effect (Z0701). A Siegel-zero case cannot occur in this range.

For fixed p, the ES solution set in (x,y,z) is the surface 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx): degree 3, dimension 2 (irreducible, since the form is not a product). No Birch-type criterion was applied; the dimension count gives no obstruction by itself.

Least C with a proper divisor d = -1 mod 4C of 4Cp+1, over p=1 mod 4 below 1e4 (609 primes): C_min=1 for 439, max 40 (at p=4789), 4 primes with none up to 200. Mean C_min/log^2 p = 0.03, consistent with C <= p^eps in this range. Uses divisors, not only prime factors.

Bilinear count sum_C #{d | 4Cp+1 : d = -1 mod 4C}: mean ratio to tau(N)/phi(4C) is 0.20 and 93.5% of (C,p) pairs have zero count (C<=50, p<3000, 10550 pairs). The divisor distribution is far from equidistributed in the classes -1 mod 4C, so the equidistribution input is not satisfied at these sizes.

Matomäki–Radziwiłł-type averages (arXiv 1501.04585, abstract read) cover short intervals and multiplicative functions in long ranges. The ES AP problem has modulus 4p and length X = p^theta with theta < 1, below the range where those results apply (modulus must be at most a small power of the length). Not applicable as stated.
Abstract read (arXiv 1107.1010, Elsholtz–Tao): sum_{p<=N} f(p) = Theta(N log^2 N) up to a log log factor. Only the first moment is in the abstract; higher moments not checked.

Exceptions to the Erdős–Straus–Schinzel conjecture (arXiv 2511.16817, read abstract): if a uniform bound n_m exists for m/n, then n_m >= exp(m^{1/3+o(1)}), and for m >= 6.5e9 there are primes p in (m^2, 2m^2) with m/p not a sum of 3 unit fractions. Uniform-in-m scaling therefore cannot give ES(p) for m=4 directly.
The 'sporadic list' of composite n with certificate incompatibilities is not defined in this batch; defining it and checking scaling compatibility needs repo data (> 30 min).

Minimal positive gap 4/p - S over S = sums of three unit fractions with x<=y<=z<=120, for p<200 (35 primes): median gap x p = 4e-5; min 3e-6. No near-solution structure visible at this M. Range p<=1e5 not run.
next: Extend to p<=1e5 with a sorted-sum search (about 30 min).

summary: No ES construction in the repo or the data has an auxiliary prime chosen freely in an AP: the Type I certificate needs a divisor in a prescribed residue class mod 4C (Z1443), not a free prime. The check was a search of the repo's construction list, not an experiment.
Push to 1e9 (about 1.6e6 hard primes) with the least-family size: each prime needs a multi-family search; the estimated run time exceeds 30 min.
next: Run the existing script in chunks over p in [1e8, 1e9].

summary: Pure reformulation: ES holds iff 4/p has a three-term decomposition, i.e. Frobenius in a union of Chebotarev sets for the divisor-class conditions. No testable statement beyond Z1443 and the Type I divisor test.

Web search (Lagarias–Montgomery–Odlyzko, least prime splitting completely in an abelian extension) gives unconditional bounds polynomial in the discriminant. Applied to the family Q(zeta_{4C}), the witness C would need to be at most polynomial in p, which the C_min data (max 40 for p<1e4) support but do not prove.
Lookup limited to least-prime-in-Chebotarev bounds (see Z0659). No pointwise sieve result of the requested form found in that search. Not a complete literature review.

Partial Spearman of residual log U with tau(p-1), controlling for L(1,chi_p) (computed via the Dirichlet L-formula), p=1 mod 4 below 6000 (n=372): -0.22 (raw -0.56). tau(p-1) stays significant, so L(1,chi_p) does not absorb it.

rho(residual log U, tau((p+3)/4)) = +0.62 for p=1 mod 4 up to 3e4 (raw 0.51). The first three x-values (x - ceil(p/4) <= 2) carry on average only 46% of solutions (median 45%, n=211 primes below 3000), so U is not concentrated at the first few x.

U mod 6 among p=1 mod 4 up to 3e4 (1600 primes): residues 0..5 at 0.161, 0.150, 0.163, 0.183, 0.168, 0.176. Bias at U=1 mod 6 is -1.8 SE. Repeated denominators do not occur for p=1 mod 4 (Z0259 lemma), so the separation step is moot.
